text:
amanda: FYI — we should refactor the sovereign-write handshake. current swap path is racy and causes tenant-level write failures during region cutovers. want to propose a simpler contract that is safer for active/active and easier to audit. :thinking_face:

raj: can you outline the main failure modes you're seeing?

amanda: sure. two classes: 1) two-region lease swap where both primaries think they hold the write lease for a short window and we end up with duplicate writes or rejects, and 2) service-level p99 spikes because proxy waits for cross-region confirmation on the hot path. also compliance wants clearer proof of consent for writes originating outside resident region.

olivia: is this a control-plane change only? or do proxies/dataplane need to be updated?

amanda: both. control plane will issue a short-lived "escrow token" when a write claim is accepted. dataplane proxies will accept write only if escrow token is present OR if a fast-fail fallback is enabled. We want to reduce synchronous cross-region RTTs for the happy path.

dennis: proposal idea: preflight claim + local-ack path. Preflight returns a lease token (opaque) and an assurance header for the proxy to continue. If claim fails, proxy can either forward to resident region or surface a 409 with a reason code. Keeps semantics explicit.

miguel: sketch of the flow that would be easy to implement in the runtime:

```
POST /v1/tenants/{tid}/claim
Headers: X-Region: eu-west-1, X-Intent: write
Body: {session_id, keyspace}
200 -> {lease_id, expires_at, escrow_token}
Proxy stores escrow_token in request context and attaches X-Escrow: <token> to write requests.
Write path checks X-Escrow; if missing, it fast-forwards to resident region or returns 409 depending on feature flag.
```

raj: +1. how do we prevent token replay or forged tokens?

amanda: tokens are HMAC-signed by control plane with a versioned key and include tid, lease_id, expiry, and origin-region. Dataplane verifies signature with the public key rotation table. No nested synchronous key fetches — proxies cache public keys for short TTL.

kate: what about telemetry? we should add metrics to track handshake latency and fallback rate. something like residency.handshake.latency, residency.handshake.failures, residency.forwarded_writes.count.

sre-bot: alert: increased residency handshake failures observed last week in eu-west; see incident 2026-03-18-eviction-warmup. :warning:

olivia: rollout plan idea: feature-flag the fast local-ack path (residency_handshake_v2). Start in beta for a handful of tenants, then canary the proxies in a single region, then expand. Also add a guardrail to refuse fast-ack for tenants with strict data residency flag until they've opted in.

dennis: test matrix we need: unit tests for token generation/verification, integration test simulating dual-claim under injected clock skew, and chaos experiment to drop cross-region control plane messages. Also add an e2e with synthetic traffic where we assert no duplicate-final-writes.

miguel: small compat note — older clients may not set X-Intent header. proxy should assume write when method==POST && path matches /v1/streams/* with a conservative fallback. document API changes in changelog.

amanda: open questions: 1) should proxy verify escrow signature or rely on control plane to attach a short-lived signed header? 2) should we support partial writes during a swap window (append-only) or be strictly linearizable?

raj: for 1) I lean proxy verify: avoids trusted-control-plane-per-hop assumption and gives better audit trail. for 2) we should be conservative: linearizable for now, append-only is a bigger semantic change.

kate: also think about the observability events we need in Console: per-tenant last-successful-lease, last-fallback, and a time-series of forwarded_writes with HTTP reason codes. operators will want easy filters.

amanda: agreed. I'll draft a short RFC with APIs, tokens, public-key rotation, metrics, and rollout checklist. Will include a small stub of verification code in go and a proxy change set. :memo:

miguel: can you add a small compatibility shim in the proxy to map older headers? saves us a follow-up.

amanda: yep. owner = amanda (control-plane token), dennis (proxy impl), olivia (product/consent gating), kate (metrics/console).

raj: timeline?

amanda: aim for RFC + tests by next Tue (6291170000), internal canary in 2 weeks, GA after successful canaries and chaos runs.

kate: :thumbsup: will add the graphs to the dashboard template.

sre-bot: note added to runbook: when handshake.failures > 0.5% for 10m, alert on-call and instantiate cross-region-verify-runbook.

amanda: thanks all — posting RFC draft in #architecture/rfcs in a few hours. please review. :eyes:
